findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction that hides website from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
findings.body: This serializer deliberately strips profile fields like `website` for TL0 users viewed anonymously via `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. The newly added `website_name` attribute is declared as a plain attribute and is not part of that mechanism, so for a restricted (e.g. spammy TL0) user the JSON payload still contains `website_name` with the website's host/path even though `website` itself is removed. That defeats the purpose of the restriction: anonymous viewers (and crawlers) still see the website domain. `website_name` should get the same guard — either add it to `untrusted_attributes` or make its inclusion conditional on `!scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so ActiveModelSerializers never calls it
findings.body: AMS conditional-inclusion hooks must be named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is always serialized — including as `null` for users with no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and, per the related finding, have it also check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` so the privacy behavior matches `website`).

findings.title: Non-ASCII (IDN) website URLs make website_name nil, hiding the user's website entirely
findings.body: Ruby's `URI()` only accepts ASCII; a website like `http://münchen.de/page` raises URI::InvalidURIError, which the inline `rescue nil` turns into a nil host, causing `website_name` to return nil. The template (`{{#if model.website_name}}`) then hides the website block completely. Previously the display name was computed client-side with `website.split('/')[2]`, which handled such URLs fine, so this is a display regression for users with internationalized domains. Consider a tolerant fallback (e.g. string splitting, or falling back to the raw website string) when URI parsing fails.

findings.title: The sibling-subdomain branch of website_name (elsif) has no test coverage
findings.body: The most intricate condition added in `website_name` — the `elsif` that strips the first DNS label of both hosts when they have the same label count (e.g. website `www.example.com` vs instance `forum.example.com`) — is not exercised by any spec. The three added tests only cover equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and the parent-domain suffix case. Add a test with `Discourse.current_hostname` returning 'forum.example.com' and website 'http://www.example.com/user' expecting 'www.example.com/user', plus a negative case (same label count, different parent, e.g. www.other.com) to lock in the comparison behavior.
